verses.1: In the sixth year of the reign of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, Nebuzaradan, king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem. He built a city there.
verses.2: And Adonai gave Yehoyakim, king of Judah, and all the items belonging to the temple of God, into his hands. He brought them to the land of Israel, to the house of God. And he also brought along all the offerings that belonged to the temple of God.
verses.3: And the king said to Ashpenaz, the great officer, “Bring from among the children of Israel, and from among the descendants of the kings, and from among the Persians.”
verses.4: Children who have no flaws at all, who are beautiful in appearance, intelligent in every way, and possess knowledge and understanding. They also have the strength to stand in the king’s palace and to teach others.
verses.5: And the king spoke to them on that day. He told them about the years of their lives, and how they would grow up. From that time onward, they would stand before the king.
verses.6: And among them were the sons of Judah: Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.
verses.7: And the chief of the priests put on them crowns. They also put Beltsazar, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah on them as decorations.
verses.8: And Daniel put it on his heart, knowing that he would not be glorified by the king’s wine or his gifts. He also asked for help from the officials of the palace, who would not be glorified either.
verses.9: And God gave Daniel mercy and compassion before the chief of the officers.
verses.10: And the captain of the soldiers said to Daniel, “I fear the king who gives you your food and drink. What will he think of you when he sees you crying like children, since you are still young and need to live under his rule.”
verses.11: And Daniel said to the leader of the guards who were in charge of Daniel’s life, “Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.”
verses.12: May You bless Your servants for twelve days. Then they shall give us food from the fruits, and we will eat. And we will drink water as well.
verses.13: And they will be seen before you, just as we are seen by those who eat the king’s food. And when you see what he does with your servants.
verses.14: And he heard their words, and he tried to endure for twelve days.
verses.15: And in those twelve days, it seems that all the children who eat the bread of the king are healthy and strong.
verses.16: And the magician took their food and wine, and gave them seeds instead.
verses.17: And these children, all four of them, received from God knowledge and wisdom in every book. Daniel understood all visions and dreams.
verses.18: And for the time that the king said they should be brought forth, the chief priests brought them before Nebuchadnezzar.
verses.19: And the king spoke to them. But among all of them, none was like Daniel Hananiah from Israel. Azariah also stood before the king.
verses.20: And all that wisdom and knowledge was sought after by the king. He found twelve people who knew everything related to the various rituals and ceremonies that took place throughout his kingdom.
verses.21: And Daniel served King Koresh for one year.
